sources.note: COMSTECH's own programme page (comstech.org) for its Research Fellowships for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in the OIC. COMSTECH is the OIC's Ministerial Standing Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation; the page is the awarding body itself, not an aggregator, news article, blog or wiki mirror.

awarding_body.detail: The page is on comstech.org, the award holder's own domain, and states the fellowships are awarded by COMSTECH with host institutions. This matches the record's OIC-COMSTECH awarding body.
awarding_body.quote: Research fellowships are awarded by COMSTECH, along with Host Institutions Joint scholarship Committee, based on scientific merit.

deadline.detail: No fixed date. The page states nominations are open all year and the call is currently open (rolling). This matches the record's rolling deadline. Cycle is open today (12 October 2026).
deadline.quote: Applications /Nominations are open all around the year

eligibility.detail: All sub-claims confirmed: citizens of an OIC least-developed country OR employed by a research institution in an OIC country; minimum M.S. (graduate studies, max age 35) or Ph.D. (post-graduate studies, max age 45) or active research; preference to young scientists, especially women, at the start of their career and those working in OIC LDCs.
eligibility.quote: Eligible applicants for the research fellowships are young scientists and Engineers who are citizens of a least developed country of OIC, or are employed by a research institution in an OIC country.

funding.detail: Consistent with 'Partially Funded'. COMSTECH covers only the international low-cost airfare; accommodation, subsistence, supervision and mentoring are only 'expected' from the host institution. No monthly stipend and no tuition are stated, and the page never claims the award is fully funded. This is a 6-12 month research/advanced-training stay, not a degree with tuition.
funding.quote: COMSTECH will bear international low-cost airfare. The host institutions are expected to provide accommodation, subsistence supervision, and mentor local trainings.

degree_levels.detail: The record says 'PhD', but the page opens the fellowship to holders of M.S. OR Ph.D.: a graduate-studies track (M.S. holders, max age 35) and a post-graduate track (Ph.D. holders, max age 45). It confers no degree. A PhD-only label is therefore too narrow. This is a classification gap, not a different deadline/funding/award/body, so it drives needs_review rather than conflicting.
degree_levels.quote: Minimum degree held M.S./Ph.D. or equivalent ... young scientists holding at least an M.S or equivalent degree for graduate studies, and Ph.D. for post-graduate studies

Funding is partial: COMSTECH pays only the international low-cost airfare and accommodation/subsistence are only 'expected' from the host (no stipend or tuition). Keep current_verification_status at needs_review until a reviewer resolves the degree_levels field.

notes_for_reviewer: Verdict is needs_review (high confidence), not active, solely because the record's degree_levels='PhD' cannot be confirmed: the official page states 'Minimum degree held M.S./Ph.D.' and describes a graduate-studies track (M.S. holders, max age 35) and a post-graduate track (Ph.D. holders, max age 45), so the fellowship is open at the Master's level too and awards no degree. The material contradiction categories (different deadline, funding, award, or body) are all absent — programme, awarding body, rolling open deadline and partial funding all match, so this is not 'conflicting'. A human should set the correct degree_levels value (e.g. 'Master's / PhD researchers' or 'Research, M.S./Ph.D. holders') and decide whether 'Partially Funded' should be reworded to describe the airfare-plus-living-coverage package.
